result.title: Do bots feel bad? Assessing empirical evidence for functional valence in LLMs
result.summary: Do LLMs have valenced states, i.e. states that feel pleasant or unpleasant? Recent empirical work has claimed to show that LLMs possess functional valenced states (e.g. ``functional pleasure and pain'' [Ren et al. 2026], ``functional emotions'' [Sofroniew et al. 2026], and ``functional welfare'' [Han et al. 2026]) that play the same causal role as valenced states in cognition and action, without necessarily being consciously experienced. But it remains unexplored how well the identified states fit the functional role of valence as understood in the philosophical and cognitive science literature. Here, I assess the current body of evidence, and argue (i) that key aspects of valence remain untested in LLMs, and (ii) that extant empirical paradigms inadequately distinguish (functional) valence from neighbouring constructs like preferences, value-judgments, valence attributions and role-play. I conclude by sketching some novel experimental approaches to better target (functional) valence itself.

AI.brief_summary: 一篇评估性论文，审视近期「LLM 具有功能性效价（functional pleasure/pain）」的实证证据，论证效价的关键方面尚未被检验，且现有范式无法把功能性效价与偏好、价值判断、效价归因和角色扮演区分开，最后提出新的实验思路。
AI.relevance_reason: 其对内部状态「因果角色」证据与混淆控制的批判，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态是否真被答案使用：如何区分真实状态使用与角色扮演、事后归因，以及如何设计对照范式。
